A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework despite renaming. All 21 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original reward-model evaluations, code-generation and mathematics experiments, ablations, and an appendix correlation analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds generator-diversity, model-transfer, compiler-reward, efficiency and human-validation results.

M1.justification: OD-based learning becomes CRPL and P-GRPO becomes CG-GRPO, retaining the three preference-pair types, Bradley–Terry training and binary correctness gate. Section 6 additionally tests ReCode combined with compiler/test-status rewards, a limited adaptation of the reward objective rather than a redesign of the core method.

E1.justification: The generator-diversity experiment introduces preference-training data containing Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct reasoning alongside Qwen-generated reasoning, broadening the represented source of reasoning examples. The coding and mathematical task families and evaluation benchmarks remain otherwise retained; LCB-RB sample-count and curation changes are principally protocol changes.

E2.justification: v3 adds DeepSeek-V3 to the reward-model comparison in Table 2 and a compiler-reward GRPO comparator in Table 5. Figure 3(c) also adds direct reward addition as a comparator. These substantially strengthen comparisons against powerful judges and alternative reward designs. The compiler comparator uses StepCoder-style rewards; the PDF does not report evaluating the complete StepCoder algorithm.

E3.justification: LCB-RB changes from 187 pairs sourced from LiveCodeBench v5 to 219 pairs sourced from v6, with human adjudication and an explicit exclusion of October 2024–February 2025 problems reserved for final code evaluation. New protocols include a 100-case judge audit, 50/50 generator mixing, and 400-step transfer and compiler-reward experiments. The principal training hyperparameters and greedy evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct-addition controls and reward-inflation trajectories, generator-style sensitivity, Qwen3 transfer, compiler-reward complementarity, token-efficiency analysis and human verification of the correlation study's judge. These address several previously untested explanations and reliability concerns. The 3B preference-pair ablation already existed in v2 Appendix A.5 and is relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v3 introduces inter-annotator agreement reporting for LCB-RB construction (Cohen's kappa 0.769) and the 100-case judge audit (kappa 0.82), together with judge–human consistency reporting. The existing chi-square significance claim is retained. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for the principal RL performance results.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the proposed model's HumanEval/HE+ scores from 86.6/81.1 to 90.9/86.0 and its reported average from 57.4 to 58.5. On the reconstructed LCB-RB, the 7B reward model scores 62.6 versus 58.28 previously; these use different benchmark instances. It now trails GPT-4-Turbo (63.7) and added DeepSeek-V3 (66.9). Training trajectories change, and Tables 4–8 add substantial results. Mathematics Table 3 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: No substantive new theorem, proof or derivation appears. v3 explicitly writes the Bradley–Terry objective already specified in v2. Its indicator-based correctness gate is mathematically equivalent to v2's multiplication by the binary outcome reward.

C1.justification: The central claims about correctness-gated reasoning rewards improving coding and generalizing to mathematics remain. v3 adds introductory claims of Qwen3 transfer and compiler-reward complementarity, explicitly claims LCB-RB is the first such coding reasoning-discrimination benchmark, and softens the abstract/conclusion's reward-model superiority language to strong performance.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning generator diversity versus supervision noise, complementary reasoning and compiler signals, and improved efficiency rather than longer generation. It expands limitations to benchmark scale and evaluation on models no larger than 7B, while retaining the long-context limitation. v2's SFT-disruption interpretation and proposed iterative self-training direction are removed.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents the existing Bradley–Terry loss and discloses 44,000 candidate outputs and 33,146 retained observations for the correlation analysis. It supplies settings for the added experiments and replaces the anonymous code-access link with the named ReCode GitHub reference. Hardware, learning rates, batch sizes, clipping settings and output-length limits remain documented as before.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially shifts from generic RL background to code-generation supervision, adding substantive comparisons with PPOCoder, StepCoder and PRL-Coder. v3 acknowledges implementation-level process supervision and positions its reasoning-process rewards as complementary, refining v2's broader characterization of earlier approaches as outcome-only. Publication-metadata updates alone are excluded from this judgment.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten around ReCode's two components. Benchmark construction becomes a separate section, discussion is reorganized, limitations become standalone, and appendix prompts are consolidated under A.6. These constitute substantial narrative and structural revision beyond renaming or added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, merges and redraws the method diagrams, redesigns the worked example, and combines previously separated preference-ablation plots in Figure 4. It adds five tables and a reward-dynamics panel, removes average bars from the preference plots, and captions the retained appendix prompts. Several plots become substantially smaller.

improvement.justification: v2 relied on automated benchmark labels and supported reward-hacking mitigation mainly through a soft-gate comparison. v3 adds human adjudication, judge validation, direct-addition controls and reward-inflation measurements, substantially strengthening measurement credibility and evidence for the central gating mechanism. Transfer, complementarity and efficiency analyses further improve the paper's support and scope assessment. Compressed plots and residual overstatements remain, notably Section 5.2's superiority wording despite Table 2, but the validation gains provide a substantial overall improvement.
